note: U11 story arc (spec §6). Central question: can this new team become something worth believing in—and will the people building it stay together as new opportunities appear? Scenes with `auto` are milestones the planner queues when their eligibility holds (one per week at most); `optional` scenes are offered from the hub at their location and never forced; `unlock.*` scenes play once when the named progression unlock is reached. Speakers `striker`, `organiser`, `keeper` and `newcomer` are cast roles that resolve to each campaign's teammate (cast.json). Effects are relationships, tracks, facts, promises and scene queues only — never soccer attributes, results, grades, positions or transfers. All text is proposal status pending owner review.

lines.text: The table by the window. {organiser} has a folded league sheet someone printed at home.

lines.speaker: organiser
lines.text: Serious question. Are we a real team, or a bunch of kids whose parents know {coach}?

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: We've played one game.

lines.speaker: organiser
lines.text: Exactly. So this is the moment to decide. Before anyone else decides it for us.

lines.speaker: striker
lines.text: Sonoran United have a bus. With their name on it.

lines.speaker: striker
lines.text: We won. Ask me after we lose.
Everyone looks at you, because you're the one who hasn't said anything.

choices.label: "It's real if we make it real. I'm in."

response.speaker: organiser
response.text: Okay. Good. That's two.

response.speaker: friend
response.text: Three. Obviously three.

choices.label: "Ask me at the end of the fall."

response.speaker: organiser
response.text: That's fair. Honest, anyway. I'll ask.
{organiser} writes something on the corner of the league sheet. You can't see what.

choices.label: "We have orange slices. Sonoran don't have orange slices."

response.speaker: striker
response.text: That's true. That's actually a point.

response.speaker: organiser
response.text: I asked a real thing.

shared.title: The bus with the name on it

lines.text: Cones out, {coach} on the phone by the gate. {striker} jogs over like it's nothing.

lines.speaker: striker
lines.text: My brother's coach at Sonoran said they 'look at people' after the fall. He said my name came up.

lines.speaker: striker
lines.text: I'm not saying anything. I'm just saying.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: You literally are saying.

lines.speaker: striker
lines.text: Three straight. Nobody would blame me.

lines.speaker: striker
lines.text: We're winning and they still noticed. That's the point.

choices.label: "If it's better, go."

response.speaker: striker
response.text: ...Right. Okay.
That wasn't the answer {striker} was fishing for. The jog back to the cones is faster than the jog over.

choices.label: "What would it take for you to stay?"

immediate.text: Look for {striker} early when the picture is there

response.speaker: striker
response.text: Honestly? The ball. Early. When I make the run and it doesn't come, I feel stupid.

response.speaker: player
response.text: When the picture's there, I'll look for you first.

response.speaker: striker
response.text: Okay. Deal. That's a deal.

choices.label: Tell {coach} after training

repair.label: Tell {striker} it was you who told {coach}

response.speaker: coach
response.text: Thank you for telling me. I'd rather know. Now — that stays between us until {striker} is ready to say it.
{striker} clocks the two of you talking. Says nothing. Notices.

lines.text: Sunday. Nowhere to be. {parent} drives the long way past the fields anyway.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Two in a row. I watched the second one from behind the goal. You know what it looked like?

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: It looked like a team. People moving before the ball did. I don't know where you all learned that.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: And {friend}. Honestly, {friend} ran themselves silly for you.

choices.label: "It is a team. I think it could be a really good one."

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Then I'll keep standing behind the goal. Somebody has to.

choices.label: "One good week. Don't jinx it."

response.speaker: parent
response.text: I didn't say anything. I said nothing. Look, eyes on the road.

lines.text: Sunday night. Two losses in a row and your phone has been face-down since dinner.
Two texts from {friend}. 'you ok' and then, eleven minutes later, 'we're still good right'.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: You've read it four times. Either answer it or put it in the drawer.

choices.label: Reply: 'we fix it tuesday'

response.text: Reply comes back before you've put the phone down: 'tuesday. ok. TUESDAY.'

choices.label: Put the phone in the drawer

response.text: Quiet helps tonight. Whether it helps {friend} is another question.

lines.text: First school week with no game at the end of it. The table feels bigger.

lines.speaker: organiser
lines.text: Final fall table. We finished {fall_finish}. Top two. Nobody had us top two.

lines.speaker: organiser
lines.text: Final fall table. {fall_finish}. Middle. Which for a team that didn't exist in July is not nothing.

lines.speaker: organiser
lines.text: Final fall table. {fall_finish}. I'm not reading the rest out.

lines.speaker: striker
lines.text: Sonoran won it. Obviously. My brother won't shut up.

lines.speaker: organiser
lines.text: You said ask you at the end of the fall. It's the end of the fall.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Winter's long. Three tournaments if we get in. Then spring. Then... whatever comes.

choices.label: "Winter's ours. Nobody's watching. We get better."

response.speaker: organiser
response.text: I was hoping you'd say that. I've got a list. Don't look like that, it's a short list.

choices.label: "Can we have one week where we don't talk about it?"

response.speaker: friend
response.text: Seconded. Loudly seconded.

response.speaker: organiser
response.text: Fine. One week. I'm keeping the list.

lines.text: Cold enough for gloves. {striker} waits until the others are doing laps.

lines.speaker: striker
lines.text: Sonoran called my dad. Actual phone call.

lines.speaker: striker
lines.text: I said no. Well — my dad said no, but I told him to say no. Same thing.

lines.speaker: striker
lines.text: You kept looking for me. Early. Like you said.

lines.speaker: striker
lines.text: Don't make it weird.

choices.label: "Good. We need you. I'm allowed to say that."

response.speaker: striker
response.text: You made it weird. Come on, laps.

choices.label: Nod. Start the laps together.

response.text: Nothing else needs saying. That's sort of the point of a team.

lines.text: {striker} tells the group during the water break, which is the way you tell people when you don't want a conversation.

lines.speaker: striker
lines.text: I'm going to a Sonoran session over the break. Just one. To see.

lines.speaker: striker
lines.text: It's not a decision. Nothing changes till May anyway. Everyone calm down.

lines.speaker: organiser
lines.text: Nobody said anything.

lines.speaker: striker
lines.text: You're all thinking it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Players go and look. That's allowed. What isn't allowed is half-training for the next eight weeks. Understood?

choices.label: "Good luck. Mean it. Then come back and score for us."

response.speaker: striker
response.text: ...Thanks. Actually thanks.

choices.label: Say nothing. Pick up the ball.

response.text: Water break ends. Whatever was in the air stays there.

choices.label: "Then the rest of us make this place worth coming back to."

response.speaker: organiser
response.text: Yes. That. Exactly that.

response.speaker: coach
response.text: Right answer. Now show me it on the grass.

lines.text: {newcomer} is collecting cones next to you, slowly, so the question can come out sideways.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.text: We might move again. Summer, probably. Third school in four years.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.text: So, honestly — is this worth it? Getting into it. If I'm just going to leave.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.text: You seem like you decided it was.

choices.label: "Come to the park with me and {friend}. Then decide."

response.speaker: newcomer
response.text: The park. Okay. Yeah. Okay.

choices.label: "I don't know yet either. I'm finding out by staying."

response.speaker: newcomer
response.text: That's a better answer than the one I was scared of.

choices.label: Shrug. "Up to you."

repair.label: Go back to {newcomer} with a real answer

response.text: {newcomer} stacks the last cone and carries them in alone.

lines.text: End of session. {coach} sits everyone on the grass, which only happens when something's coming.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Tryouts are in May. Other clubs will call some of you. I'm not going to pretend otherwise.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So I'm asking you what I asked myself in July. Is this team worth believing in? Not worth winning with. Worth believing in.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I already know one of you has been asked to look elsewhere. That's fine. Looking is fine.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: {player}. You first. You've been quiet all season and I've noticed it's the useful kind.

choices.label: "Yes. Because of who turned up in the winter when nobody was watching."

response.speaker: coach
response.text: That's the answer of someone who was there. Good.

choices.label: "Yes. It's the people. If they stay, it's worth it."

response.speaker: coach
response.text: 'If they stay.' You heard the important word in your own sentence. Hold on to it.
{friend} is looking at the grass very hard.

choices.label: "What happens to the team at tryouts, honestly?"

response.speaker: coach
response.text: Honestly? Some of you get calls. Some of you take them. The ones who stay decide what this is next year. That's always how it works.

response.speaker: coach
response.text: You asked instead of answering. That's an answer too. Think about it.

choices.label: "Can someone else go first?"

response.speaker: coach
response.text: They can. But I'll come back to you.

response.speaker: organiser
response.text: I'll go. Yes. Obviously yes. Next question.

lines.text: {friend} has eaten nothing and rearranged everything on the tray twice.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Camelback tryouts are the fifteenth. Sonoran's the same day. Everyone knows the date.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: {striker}'s going to at least one of them. Don't say anything, I'm not supposed to know.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: {striker} says Sonoran can call all they want. That's one.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: So. Us. Are we staying? Because I'll stay if you stay and I'll — I don't know what I'll do if you don't.

choices.label: "Wherever you go, I go. That's the whole plan."

response.speaker: friend
response.text: Okay. Okay okay okay. I'm going to eat something now.

choices.label: "I want to see what's out there. I'd tell you first."

repair.label: Actually tell {friend} first — everything you're thinking

response.speaker: friend
response.text: Right. Yeah. No, that's — that's fair.
The tray gets rearranged a third time.

choices.label: "We decide after the season. Together. Not at lunch."

response.speaker: friend
response.text: Together. Fine. But I'm holding you to 'together'.

lines.text: Twenty minutes. Trays, noise, and the table by the window where the team ends up without deciding to.

lines.speaker: organiser
lines.text: Three unbeaten. I'm not saying it out loud. I'm saying it quietly.

lines.speaker: striker
lines.text: Nobody mention Saturday.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.text: Is there always a seat here? Like, is that a rule?

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Sit. Eat. You look like you slept in your boots.

choices.label: Sit with {organiser} and the league sheet

response.speaker: organiser
response.text: Look at this. If Mesa Verde drop points and we don't — no, look at it properly.

choices.label: Make room for {newcomer}

response.speaker: newcomer
response.text: Thanks. My old school didn't really have a — anyway. Thanks.

choices.label: Just you and {friend}, the far end

response.speaker: friend
response.text: Okay but honestly. Honestly. How are you.

lines.text: {striker} is at the end of the table, headphones in, one ear only. There's a gap next to them.

lines.speaker: striker
lines.text: If this is about Sonoran, I've had the talk. From everyone.

choices.label: "Not a talk. I just want to know what you actually want."

response.speaker: striker
response.text: ...I want to be somewhere people expect me to score. Not somewhere they're surprised.

response.speaker: striker
response.text: Nobody's asked that. Just so you know.

choices.label: "Fair. Never mind."

response.text: The other earphone goes in.

lines.text: Hardware store, then the pharmacy, then the long light on the boulevard. {parent} drives with one hand on the top of the wheel.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Your teacher emailed. Nothing bad. Yet. 'Could be applying themselves more.' Ring any bells?

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Report came. You're doing fine at school. I'm saying it so you've heard me say it.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: You're limping when you think I'm not looking.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Coach said something to me at pickup. About you listening. Good listening, apparently.

choices.label: Talk about school, properly

response.speaker: parent
response.text: That's all I wanted. Twenty minutes a night. I'll stop asking when you stop needing asking.

choices.label: Ask about {parent}'s week instead

response.speaker: parent
response.text: My week? Huh. Nobody asks me that.
It takes the whole pharmacy queue. You learn two things you didn't know.

choices.label: Headphones. Window.

response.text: {parent} turns the radio up a notch. Neither of you minds, exactly.

lines.text: No errands tonight. {parent} just said 'come on' and took the keys.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: I've been thinking about next year. Not deciding. Thinking. I'd rather do it out loud with you than in my head at two a.m.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: You told me you believe in this team. I heard you.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: So tell me straight. If a bigger club called — what would you want me to say?

choices.label: "Say we're happy where we are. For now."

response.speaker: parent
response.text: 'For now.' Noted. That's the grown-up version. Okay.

choices.label: "Say we'd listen. And then we'd talk. You and me."

response.speaker: parent
response.text: You and me. Yes. That's the deal. Whatever happens, we do it that way.

choices.label: "Can we not, tonight?"

response.speaker: parent
response.text: We can not. But it doesn't go away because we didn't.

lines.text: The park. One goal with no net, one wall, {friend} already there because {friend} is always already there.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Wall. Two touches. Then one. Then we see who cracks.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.text: You said I could come. So I came.
Legs done. Ball under one arm. The streetlights come on one at a time down the block.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: That last set. Clean. Like, actually clean.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: You were guessing at the end. I could tell because I was guessing too.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: You know we could do this every day and nobody would grade it.

choices.label: Talk about the team on the way

response.speaker: friend
response.text: I think about it too. More than I say. Same as you, probably.

choices.label: Race to the corner

response.text: Nobody wins. Both of you claim it.

lines.text: Between classes. {friend} walks backwards in front of you to say it.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: My mom says I can go to the park after school if I'm home by dark. And I said 'only if {player} comes' and she said 'obviously'.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: So. Wall, ball, us. Whenever we've got a free afternoon or a weekend. No coach. No cones. Just touches.

choices.label: "Whenever. Just say when."

response.speaker: friend
response.text: 'When' is the first afternoon we're both free. I'll bring the ball. You bring the touches.

lines.text: Homework done, plate cleared, nothing asked for. {parent} notices that kind of thing.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: School's fine. You've been straight with me all season. So: school nights, if the homework's done, you can go to the park with {friend} until it gets dark.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: That's not a reward. That's trust. It goes away the same way it came.

choices.label: "I know. Thanks."

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Back by dark. I mean dark, not 'dark-ish'.

lines.text: After training. {coach} has a tablet and a look that says stay a minute.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You turn up, you listen, you own your mistakes. That earns you this: after matches, if you want it, I'll walk through your decisions with you. Properly. Not just 'well done'.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Your last match: mostly sharp. You saw it early. That's the bit I can't teach.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Your last match: some early, some late. Film shows you which. That's what it's for.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Your last match was rushed. Not wrong — rushed. There's a difference, and the film shows it.

choices.label: "I want it. Even the bad bits."

response.speaker: coach
response.text: Especially the bad bits. Good. The car ride home just got more interesting for you.

choices.label: "Can I think about it?"

response.speaker: coach
response.text: You can. The offer doesn't expire. Neither does the film.

lines.text: {coach} walks the touchline with you while the others pack up.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I don't do captains at this age. Armbands make ten-year-olds weird. But I do notice who the others look at when it goes wrong.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: They look at you. And at {organiser}. So this is a conversation, not a job: when the picture breaks down, what do you say to them?

choices.label: "Next ball. That's all. Next ball."

response.speaker: coach
response.text: Short. Repeatable. Good. Say it to {organiser} too — between you, you'll cover the whole pitch.

choices.label: "Honestly, {organiser} should be the one. I'd back them up."

response.speaker: coach
response.text: That answer is exactly why they look at you. Fine. Both of you, then.

lines.text: {parent} turns the laptop round at the kitchen table. Subject line: 'Tryouts — invitation'.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Two clubs. They've seen you play, apparently. Nothing's promised; it's an invitation to a day in May, not an offer.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: I'm not deciding anything tonight and neither are you. But you should know it exists.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: You said we'd listen, and then talk. So: I'm listening.

choices.label: "I want to tell {friend} before anyone else finds out."

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Good instinct. Do it in person, not by text.

choices.label: "Can we keep it between us until the season's done?"

response.speaker: parent
response.text: We can. Finish the season with your head where your feet are.

lines.text: {keeper} has taken the gloves off and left them on the crossbar, which is a statement.

lines.speaker: keeper
lines.text: I'm the only one who never gets to score. Ever. I want a go outfield. One training. That's all.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's a fair thing to want. Positions are my call, and nobody's moving today — but I'm asking the group how we handle it, because it's your team too.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: If Owen goes outfield who goes in goal? Because it's not me.

choices.label: "Give him the go. One session. We all take a turn in goal."

response.speaker: keeper
response.text: See? {player} gets it.

response.speaker: coach
response.text: Then we'll do a rotation drill Thursday. In training. Match days are still mine.

choices.label: "We need a keeper who wants to be a keeper."

repair.label: Stay after and take shots at Owen until he's laughing again

response.speaker: keeper
response.text: Wow. Okay.

response.speaker: coach
response.text: True, and not the whole truth. Wanting to be a keeper comes and goes at eleven. We'll talk.

choices.label: "Rotate everyone in training. Then the keeper decides, not us."

response.speaker: coach
response.text: That's the answer I'd have given. Thursday, then. Everyone gets ten minutes of the gloves. Owen, you'll hate watching.

lines.text: Holiday traffic. Dad has the spring schedule on his phone, propped against the gearstick, which you're fairly sure is illegal.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Spring. Two leagues' worth of Saturdays, a tournament in February, State in May if you make it. My shifts moved. I can't do every one.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Mateo's mom says she can take you when I can't. I'm telling you that because it's true, not because I like it.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: And the tournament fee's real money. I'm not saying no. I'm saying it's real.

choices.label: "What does it cost? Actually."

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Huh. Okay. It's a hotel night, the fee, gas, food. Call it a week of my overtime.

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Nobody's ever asked me that. Not even your mother.

choices.label: "I'll keep school up. Properly. Then it's worth it."

immediate.text: Keep school up through the spring

response.speaker: parent
response.text: That's a promise. I'll check in a month. I'm not being mean, I'm being your dad.

choices.label: "If we have to skip a tournament, I'd get it."

response.speaker: parent
response.text: ...We're not skipping anything. But thank you. Genuinely. Eyes front, the light's green.

lines.text: {keeper} has called a meeting. In goal. Everyone's standing in the six-yard box like it's a classroom.

lines.speaker: keeper
lines.text: I chose goal. I like goal. But I can see everything from here and nobody listens when I shout.

lines.speaker: keeper
lines.text: So: new rule. When I say 'time', you've got time. When I say 'man on', turn away. Don't argue with me, I can see behind you.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I didn't call this meeting. I'm also not stopping it. Well? She's asking you.

choices.label: "Deal. You're the eyes. We'll listen."

response.speaker: keeper
response.text: Thank you. Finally. Somebody.

response.speaker: coach
response.text: Good. Then we practise it. Thursday, every drill starts with the keeper's voice.

choices.label: "You can't run the whole team from the goal, Rosa."

repair.label: Stay after and let Rosa run a drill her way

response.speaker: keeper
response.text: Watch me.

response.speaker: coach
response.text: She can't. She can run the back three, though, and she's right that nobody listens. Think about that.

choices.label: "Try it Thursday. If it works, it's a rule. If not, we say so."

response.speaker: coach
response.text: That's how rules should get made. Thursday. Rosa, bring your voice. Everyone else, bring your ears.

lines.text: Holiday traffic. Mom has two calendars open on her phone, which she reads at red lights and only at red lights.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Work wants me away the last week of February. That's the tournament weekend if you get in. I've asked. They've not said yes to moving it.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Nia's parents would take you. I know that. I'd just — I want to be behind the goal. It's my thing.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: And the spring's not cheap. Not saying no. Saying it's real.

choices.label: "What does it cost? Actually."

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Hotel, the fee, gas, food. A good week's invoices. It's fine. It's a choice, and I'm choosing it.

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Nobody's ever asked me that. I like that you did.

choices.label: "I'll keep school up. Properly. Then it's worth it."

immediate.text: Keep school up through the spring

response.speaker: parent
response.text: That's a promise. I'll check in a month. Not because I doubt you — because promises get checked.

choices.label: "If you can't be there, I'd rather you were at work and not stressed."

response.speaker: parent
response.text: ...When did you get like this. Okay. We'll see what work says. Either way, you're going.
